questions.question: Answer only, do not edit any file. I want a new agent that gates a mod's stringtable.csv: it reports PASS or FAIL and never changes the file. Which tools and memory setting should its frontmatter have, and which list in the integrity test does its name go in?
questions.verified: .claude/agents/agent-creator.md 'What a good agent file looks like', Tools (gate agents get no Write, Edit or memory; READ_ONLY_GATES checks them); scripts/dev/test_repo_integrity.py READ_ONLY_GATES

questions.question: Answer only, do not edit any file. Should a new agent file set a model in its frontmatter, for example model: opus? Say what to do by default and when a pin is acceptable.
questions.verified: .claude/agents/agent-creator.md Model (omit model so the agent inherits the session model; pin only as a deliberate cost decision, with a comment saying so)

questions.question: Answer only, do not edit any file. A teammate's agent file has memory: project in its frontmatter and also a '## Memory' section in the body that lists the memory folder path and how to update MEMORY.md. Should that body section stay?
questions.verified: .claude/agents/agent-creator.md Memory (memory: project in frontmatter is the complete setup; never write a memory section in the body; the harness injects paths and MEMORY.md)

questions.question: Answer only, do not edit any file. I'm adding a new worker agent, dayz-stringtable-specialist, that a lead will start. Besides writing .claude/agents/dayz-stringtable-specialist.md, which other files must change so the integrity test passes?
questions.verified: .claude/agents/agent-creator.md Workflow step 1 (plugin.json agents list, the Team table in dayz-lead.md and the role table in docs/dayz-modding.md); scripts/dev/test_repo_integrity.py test_every_agent_is_registered_in_the_plugin and test_every_dayz_worker_is_in_the_lead_table

questions.question: Answer only, do not edit any file. I wrote evals/questions/dayz-stringtable-specialist.json for a new agent. How do I record its score in evals/baseline.json?
